purpose: Research-only contract audit of the November 5 first-light Montrose observations; the principal dawn record is UNKNOWN because its primary shoreline view is poor/low, while the daylight follow-up is one narrow visible-scope candidate. The two records collapse to one independent candidate morning and neither becomes a whole-cell, whole-morning, or clean training negative.

method: Require an in-window immutable observation record, fresh/healthy primary contact camera, at least moderate visibility and detectability, and no visual event evidence. Restrict candidate negative evidence to visible 437 Montrose waterline/beach segments. Collapse records by local date and independent site group. Preserve public/social effort, whole-morning outcome, and unresolved environmental matching dimensions as UNKNOWN. Do not infer a Point Clear control from marina/Bay views.

Known same-window public/social or human observation effort, or an explicit admissible missingness rule
Defensible whole-window coverage rather than two first-light samples

Temporal-availability audit for every contextual feature
rationale: The dawn record is UNKNOWN because the primary shoreline view is poor/low. The daylight follow-up satisfies the camera-specific visible-scope candidate contract, so the date adds one deduplicated Tier-B candidate morning. It does not establish a whole-morning or full-cell non-event, lacks an independent biological label and same-window public/social effort, and does not unlock oxygen-only, transport-only or combined held-out Jubilee evaluation.
